q: Are steel pipes, tubes and pipe fittings covered by EU CBAM?
title: Are steel pipes covered by CBAM?
short: Yes. Cast iron pipes (7303), pipes made without a weld (7304), large welded pipes (7305), other welded and hollow profiles (7306) and pipe fittings such as flanges, elbows and couplings (7307) are all in Annex I of the CBAM Regulation. Valves and hoses are classified elsewhere and are not covered today.
audience: Steel pipe, tube and fitting makers exporting to the EU

ul: 7303: tubes, pipes and hollow profiles of cast iron, including ductile iron pipe.
7304: tubes and pipes made without a weld, of iron or steel, including stainless.
7305: welded pipes with an external diameter over 406.4 mm.
7306: other tubes, pipes and hollow profiles, such as ERW pipe and square or rectangular hollow sections.
7307: tube or pipe fittings of iron or steel, cast or forged.
Flexible tubing and hoses of plastics or rubber.
Pipes of copper, which sit in chapter 74, outside Annex I.

p: ERW and welded pipe makers buy hot-rolled coil, and makers of pipe without a weld buy rounds or billets. These are precursors, so their embedded emissions are added to your own direct emissions from reheating, annealing and galvanising. Get the coil or billet supplier's embedded emissions per tonne for the same period. Electricity is not counted for steel goods in the definitive period.
Zinc is not a CBAM precursor, but the fuel your galvanising bath and drying ovens burn is part of your direct emissions. Meter or estimate it per tonne of pipe.

The European Commission proposed in December 2025 to extend CBAM to certain downstream products made largely of steel and aluminium. As of October 2026 that proposal is not law. Until it is adopted, coverage is what Annex I lists today, so check Annex I again before each contract season.
